## Writeups

### CTF

- [CSCBE24 - Bad Ransomware](https://bytebl33d.github.io/writeups/ctf/cscbe-bad-ransomware.md): Ransomware attacks are becoming more common every day. This forensics challenge goes in depth into the solution of the 'Bad Ransomware' challenge of the CSCBE24 Qualifiers dealing with a Known Plain-Text Attack on an encrypted zip archive.
- [Hack The Boo 2023 - Forensics and Web](https://bytebl33d.github.io/writeups/ctf/htboo-forensics-reversing.md): For this years halloween I decided to participate in the Hack The Boo CTF competition from Hack the Box. Despite this being my first solo public CTF competition, I still managed to climb to leaderboards and reach top 50 (48th to be exact).
- [HTB University CTF 2023: Brains & Bytes](https://bytebl33d.github.io/writeups/ctf/htb-university-ctf-23.md): Tasked with defending the antidote's research, a diverse group of students united against a relentless cyber onslaught. As codes clashed and defenses were tested, their collective effort stood as humanity's beacon, inching closer to safeguarding the research for the cure with every thwarted attack.

### HackTheBox

#### Machines

- [Administrator (Medium)](https://bytebl33d.github.io/writeups/hackthebox/machines/administrator.md): Administrator is a medium-difficulty Windows machine designed around a complete domain compromise scenario, where credentials for a low-privileged user are provided.
- [Blazorized (Hard)](https://bytebl33d.github.io/writeups/hackthebox/machines/blazorized.md): Blazorized is a Windows machine, starting with a website written using the Blazor .NET framework that allows downloading a DLL file that can be reverse engineered to find a JWT secret and use it to get access to the admin panel.
- [Checker (Hard)](https://bytebl33d.github.io/writeups/hackthebox/machines/checker.md): Checker is a hard-level Linux machine running Teampass and Bookstack on separate ports. The Teampass version has a SQL injection vulnerability CVE-2023-1545 that can be exploited to obtain user password hashes.
- [DarkCorp (Insane)](https://bytebl33d.github.io/writeups/hackthebox/machines/darkcorp.md): DarkCorp is an Insane-difficulty Windows machine with several computers joined. The initial foothold involves exploiting CVE-2024-42009, an XXS vulnerability and IDOR in RoundCube, via the Contact Page to read emails from a developer and leak a hidden, password-protected Analytics dashboard.
- [Infiltrator (Insane)](https://bytebl33d.github.io/writeups/hackthebox/machines/infiltrator.md): Infiltrator is an Insane Windows Active Directory machine that starts with a website that an attacker can scrape for possible usernames on the machine. One user doesn't have Kerberos pre-authentication enabled, and his password can be cracked.
- [Office (Hard)](https://bytebl33d.github.io/writeups/hackthebox/machines/office.md): The "Office" machine on HackTheBox is a challenging Windows-based environment that incorporates a variety of vulnerabilities. These include exploiting a
- [TheFrizz (Medium)](https://bytebl33d.github.io/writeups/hackthebox/machines/thefrizz.md): TheFrizz is a medium-difficulty Windows machine featuring a web application showcasing Walkerville Elementary School and a Gibbon CMS instance. The
- [University (Insane)](https://bytebl33d.github.io/writeups/hackthebox/machines/university.md): University is an Insane Windows Active Directory machine that starts with a university webpage. The web application allows exporting user profile pages to a PDF using xhtml2pdf, which is vulnerable to a Remote Code Execution vulnerability via CVE-2023-33733.
- [Vintage (Hard)](https://bytebl33d.github.io/writeups/hackthebox/machines/vintage.md): Vintage is a hard difficulty Windows machine designed around an assumed breach scenario, where the attacker is provided with low-privileged user credentials.
- [Yummy (Hard)](https://bytebl33d.github.io/writeups/hackthebox/machines/yummy.md): Yummy is a hard box that starts with a Restaurant web app using Caddy web service, on port 80, where an attacker finds an arbitrary file read HTTP Location header, which is not handled and sanitized properly by the default Caddy configuration.

#### Sherlocks

- [ProcNet (Hard)](https://bytebl33d.github.io/writeups/hackthebox/sherlocks/procnet.md): With the increasing use of open-source Command and Control (C2) frameworks by threat actors, it has become crucial for blue teams to develop strategies to detect and mitigate these threats.

- [Anti-Virus Evasion with Sliver C2](https://bytebl33d.github.io/blog/sliver-evasion.md): My recent exploration into C2 frameworks led me to BishopFox's Sliver project. - [Active Directory Home Lab with Proxmox - Part 1](https://bytebl33d.github.io/blog/proxmox-homelab-part1.md): In this post, I'll walk you through setting up my personal homelab - a project that serves both as a hands-on learning experience and as a future
- [Attacking JSON Web Tokens](https://bytebl33d.github.io/blog/jwt-attacks.md): Incorrect handling of JSON Web Tokens (JWTs) can leave a website vulnerable to a variety of attacks. To understand these attacks we first have to know what a JWT token is.
- [Web Fuzzing with FFUF](https://bytebl33d.github.io/blog/web-fuzzing-with-ffuf.md): Fuzzing is "the art of automatic bug finding", as described by the OWASP community. It is the act of sending various types of input in HTTP requests, trying to find an input or payload that causes the application to respond in unexpected ways and reveal a vulnerability.
